description:
EarthEcho: From Orbit, All the Way Down to the Field

Frontier Zero is a team of six university students from Bangladesh building EarthEcho for the Field Shift challenge, a bilingual (English and Bengali) web app that turns NASA Earth data into plain-language crop, irrigation and flood guidance for farmers. We bring web development, data analysis, AI and design, and welcome people in agriculture, Earth science and storytelling.
summary: EarthEcho turns NASA satellite data into plain-language farm decisions. A farmer marks his plot on a real satellite map, and EarthEcho reads NASA data for that exact spot. It then gives him: My Farm (saved plots), weather forecasts with farm-work advice, irrigation timing (irrigate or wait), crop suitability scores from 0 to 100, a rotation planner comparing the best rotations for his goal (save water, earn more, improve soil, lower risk), soil and NASA map layers, disaster watch (earthquakes, floods, storms, rivers), market prices, nearby suppliers, a "How sure are we?" view showing what is measured, assumed, or missing, data sources for every number, and an assistant that answers questions in Bengali or English. It answers the Field Shift challenge by replacing outdated weather assumptions with current, place-specific evidence. It always shows its sources, gaps, and risks, so the farmer stays in charge. Built by six students from Bangladesh, it works in English and Bengali, on phone and computer, for farmers everywhere.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

EarthEcho helps a farmer decide what to grow and when to act on his own plot. He marks his land on a real satellite map, and EarthEcho reads NASA data for that exact spot. It gives him irrigation timing (irrigate or wait), a 0-100 suitability score for each crop, and a rotation planner that compares the best crop rotations for his goal: save water, earn more, improve soil, or lower risk. It also includes weather, disaster watch, soil and NASA map layers, market prices, nearby suppliers, and an assistant that answers questions in Bengali or English.

HOW IT WORKS

The app takes the plot's coordinates and reads NASA POWER (weather), SMAP (soil moisture), GPM IMERG (rain), MODIS NDVI through GIBS (crop greenness) and NASA EONET (hazard alerts). It combines this with crop and soil knowledge and turns the result into short, plain-language advice. Every number shows its source, and a "How sure are we?" view separates what is measured, what is assumed and what is missing. EarthEcho does not forecast yields.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Farmers still choose crops using weather patterns that no longer hold, while satellites watch their fields every day and that data never reaches them. EarthEcho brings that data to the farmer in his own language, free to use, and specific to his plot. We will start with farmers and agriculture officers in Bangladesh, learn what fields need, then reach farms worldwide. Planned next, not built yet: GRACE-FO groundwater, ECOSTRESS plant stress, NISAR radar, and phone alerts.

TOOLS

React 19, Vite and MapLibre GL, hosted on Vercel. Live app: https://earth-echo-nine.vercel.app/ Source code: https://github.com/ArmanAhmedMiraj/EarthEcho

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It turns raw satellite data into decisions a farmer can act on, in plain Bengali or English, and it is honest about uncertainty instead of hiding it.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Language and literacy, phone use in rural areas, trust (every number links to its source), and keeping the farmer, not the app, in control of the final decision.
